chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated to me, from 'Urwah, the son of Shu'ayb's sister, al-'Aqarqufi, from his maternal uncle Shu'ayb, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said:
“Whoever becomes hungry, let him perform wudu (ablution) and pray two rak'ahs, then say: ‘O my Lord, I am hungry, so feed me.’ For indeed, he will be fed from that very hour.”
ai.seo_question: What should a person do in Islam when they are hungry and in need of food?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches turning to Allah through taharah, salat, and du'a at a moment of need. It presents hunger as an occasion for worshipful reliance upon Allah, with the promise of swift provision.
